en: Of the infidel, the ogre's son,
Then Sarybay
Was seized by his blood-drinking frenzy,
All who looked on were astonished,
No one remained unhurried,
His wrath became a grievous force,
Then Sarybay,
His eyes reddening like fire,
Swelled with menace and strained for battle,
Taking up his slaughtering steel spear,
The raging madman,
With a steel mace as large as a house,
His bloodthirsty eyes rolling,
Glowering, his hair bristling,
He began the quarrel with a deep growl,
Such again was Sarybay,
A man fully prepared for battle,
Those who heard with ears and saw with eyes
Called him Sarybay the Devourer,
Toward the poor and powerless,
He seemed never to look back,
Ready now, in his madness,
To consume the entire world,
His aspect strange, his venom strong,
“If you see his wrath, I am dead,” they said,
“Abandon hope for your precious life,”
His thoroughbred horse was Tookyzyld,
He saddled Tookyzyld,
Arranged his arms and armor,
And buckled on his flashing sword,
When the bloodthirsty man reared for battle,
His appearance utterly transformed,
He seemed ready to drive the whole world
Before him and slaughter it,
His shaggy hair stood bristling,
Then its wild rising subsided,
A hazy crimson fire
Scattered all around,
He screamed, pouring out his wrath,
Making the wrestlers flatten their ears,
And now committed a dreadful deed:
“My name is Sarybay,
Let harsh affliction be revealed,
Let blood and gore pour from combat,
Do not go on living—pass away,
Without leaving a single one,
Go and slaughter one another!
My mighty men, my warriors,
My lions who stand beside me,
Bold men girded for war,
Who destroy all they confront,
My champions, my finest men,
Those masterfully skilled with spears,
Stalwarts accomplished in cunning!”
Thus speaking, Sarybay
Set the battle order firmly,
Mounted his thoroughbred Tookyzyld,
Knotted its slender tail tight,
And, furious and prepared,
Drove out all his army,
The raging foe raised a clamor,
The sky resounded with the din,
The earth shook and mountains moved,
Piercing war cries arose,
Utter and final was the great conflict,
And mortals despaired of life,
The fierce fury of the swine,
His savage madness, became apparent,
Then Sarybay,
His eyes like hollows in a ravine,
Seemed ready to swallow his challenger,
To slaughter whoever he charged,
To ruin whoever crossed him,
And utterly wipe them out—
Such was the sight of his wrath,
He was a champion, a bulwark,
Sarybay was a mighty wrestler,
Who spared no life when grappling,
Who could not be sated with a colt's flesh,
Who mangled whoever crossed him,
And truly inflicted torment
On every mortal who confronted him,
Driving an army of tens of thousands,
He gathered all who remained
From among the dead and drove them on,
Whichever side met him was destroyed,
As he advanced and unleashed conflict,
A red haze rose like fire,
A great conflict of dire affliction,
Left every mortal full of regret,
That swift slave Sarybay,
A wicked slave in all he sought,
A baleful slave in all he observed,
His fury and lionheartedness
Surpassed all the world,
Such was that infidel's courage,
Breaking away from the host,
He appeared like Ala-Too,
He rode out raging to single combat,
The madman who scorched the earth
Charged possessed onto the battlefield,
As though to suck dry whoever crossed him,
As though to slaughter all who opposed him,
Like a mighty, merciless wrestler,
As though to tear any soul he met into ten pieces,
And mangle it again and again,
Such was his appearance,
For single combat in the great battle,
Sarybay rode out alone,
His menace unmatched, his venom strong,
“If you see the infidel, I am dead,” they said,
“Abandon hope for your precious life!”
His balefulness was unlike any other,
This terror surpassed them all,
At the ground where battle would be waged,
At the place where he would ride out alone,
He surged and thundered in frenzy,
Behind him the wrestlers
Beat their drums,
And pounded their kettledrums,
The earth split and dust arose,
Strength deserted humankind,
The countless army dared not advance,
No mortal dared show his face,
His nature strange, his venom strong—
Such was the swine Sarybay,
The scheming madman
Took up a strange long spear,
Buckled his sword diagonally,
And readied all his arms,
Like a cloud driven by a gale,
His wrath wheeled across his face,
He was a giant of mighty spirit,
Shallow in reason and without sense,
An arrogant brute,
A master of swift assaults,
A stalwart who ravaged the earth,
The wrathful infidel,
The hero of potent venom,
Rode onto the field with a roar,
Straining like a blue tiger,
Girded with blue-gray steel,
Before the hero's menace,
Most men hid themselves,
His splendid bearing became a terror,
His eyes dimmed as strength filled him,
He screamed like a scourge,
Calling for someone to ride out alone:
“Come, your lion favored by fortune!
Come, your stalwart hero, fully armed!
Come, you who level the great spear!
Come, you who deliver into my hands
The punishment of whoever advances!
Come, your lion of surpassing courage!
Come, your ready wrestler and hero!
Come, you who stand beneath the banner!
Come, satisfy the itching place,
And thrust your spear without delay!
Come, your warrior and your lion!
Come, your wrestler and your hero!
Come, you who slash and wage battle!
Come, you who finish all you seize
And tear their ribs apart!
Let the few remaining and the many come!
Let your hero come and leave no regrets!
My wrath has risen; I stand rigid,
I desire only to level my spear,
Whoever meets me shall die,
I shall put your women in black headdresses,
I shall vanquish your great ones,
I shall devour your weak,
Your wrestlers and your heroes—
I shall gouge out their eyes,
I who ruin nations and slaughter peoples,
I am Sarybay!
When I charge in fury,
I shall richly grease my sword,
I shall chew up the whole world, sparing none,
Yesterday you sorely provoked my rage,
I shall lay waste to all, leaving not a hair,
My wrath has risen; I stand rigid,
If you come out to clash, I transform,
If you enter the field, I go mad,
I mangle whoever crosses me,
I am the black scourge itself,
Gnawing whoever I encounter,
I am the black eye of the scourge,
I embody every kind of horror,
When I devour, blood cannot sate me,
When I grapple, I spare no life,
I am the black scourge itself,
You cannot go on swaggering about,
Stirring up quarrels for sport,
Why do you not restrain your courage?
How many troops have you killed?
Why have you roused this madness?
I shall overturn your burden,
My raging frenzy has seized me,
I shall not spare one of you,
I shall enslave your people,
Such is the nature of battle,
I shall destroy your lives,
I shall exhaust every stratagem,
I shall turn aside
Your flowing river,
I shall break your backs,
I shall chill your breath,
If you are a hero, be one like me—
I shall knock the wind from you,
I shall drench your banner in blood,
I shall silence your clamor at one stroke,
If I toy with you, you will not recover,
Your lumbering frenzy will not subside,
I shall master your clever one,
I shall defeat your champion,
The sly Kyrgyz have grown insolent—
I shall settle all their accounts together,
I shall slaughter them, sparing not a hair,
You have provoked my rage, you wretches,
I shall kill many of your lions!”
Thus spoke Sarybay,
Taking the form of a night-devouring fiend,
The swine spoke with a roar,
Shouting menacingly,
“Come here to confront me!” he cried,
Calling out the heroes,
His eyes like the hollows of a lake,
As though he would suck dry any soul he saw,
Such was his splendid appearance,
Whichever way you looked at him,
He seemed like a dragon lying coiled,
Ready to reduce the whole wide world to dust,
Driving it before him and swallowing it,
Tall of stature and broad of shoulder,
A monstrous wrestler, a great affliction,
Dark and formidable, fit to face a hero,
He taunted the army and called them out,
Standing there and speaking these words,
When you looked at Sarybay,
He seemed to constrict the age itself,
And make precious heads grow old,
As though in this wretched world
He alone would become its master,
As though he would drive and devour
The entire wide world,
Crushing every feeble soul,
The madman fancied himself
Ready to slaughter them and unleash conflict,
As though, with none left to oppose him,
He would become the master
Of all eighteen thousand worlds,
Such was the madman's state,
As though he would shatter the whole world,
Driving all before him and slaughtering them.
With his hair bristling wildly,
With his mane like a famished boar’s,
